extracted.intended_audience: U.S. employers, petitioners, agents, and immigration practitioners preparing or adjudicating H-class (H-1B, H-1C, H-2A, H-2B, H-3) petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and documentary criteria for filing, qualifying, and maintaining H-class nonimmigrant petitions (including H-1B specialty occupations, H-1C nurses, H-2A agricultural workers, H-2B, and H-3). Covers beneficiary and petitioner eligibility, required evidence, licensure rules, inspections, and special-category rules (physicians, fashion models, DOD projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple beneficiaries (general rule up to 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 25 named beneficiaries may be included in an H-1C, H-2A, H-2B, or H-3 petition if the beneficiaries will be performing the same service, or receiving the same training, for the same period, and in the same location. If more than 25 named beneficiaries are being petitioned for, an additional petition is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when beneficiaries perform identical services/training in same period/location. If >25 named beneficiaries, file an additional petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B, H-1C, and H-3 petitions must include the name of each beneficiary. Except as provided, all H-2A and H-2B petitions must include the name of each beneficiary who is currently in the United States, but need not name any beneficiary who is not currently in the United States. Unnamed beneficiaries must be shown on the petition by total number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may require naming H-2B beneficiaries where the name is needed to establish eligibility. If all beneficiaries under a temporary labor certification are not identified at filing, multiple petitions for subsequent beneficiaries may be filed at different times but must include a copy of the same temporary labor certification and reference previously filed petitions associated with that certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A special criteria cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Special criteria for admission, extension, and maintenance of status apply to H-2A petitions and are specified in paragraph (h)(5) of this section. The other provisions of §214.2(h) apply to H-2A only to the extent that they do not conflict with the special agricultural provisions in paragraph (h)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat H-2A provisions as having priority where they conflict with general H rules; see paragraph (h)(5) for H-2A specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of registered nurse for H-1C
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of H-1C classification, the term 'registered nurse' means a person who is or will be authorized by a State Board of Nursing to engage in registered nurse practice in a state or U.S. territory or possession, and who is or will be practicing at a facility which provides health care services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered nurse status depends on State Board authorization and practice at a qualifying health-care-providing facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility eligibility for H-1C petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A United States employer which provides health care services is referred to as a facility. A facility may file an H-1C petition for an alien nurse to perform the services of a registered nurse, if the facility meets the eligibility standards of 20 CFR 655.1111 and the other requirements of the Department of Labor's regulations in 20 CFR part 655, subpart L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioning facility must meet DOL attestation/eligibility standards referenced (20 CFR part 655, subpart L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Position requirement for H-1C
rubrics_metrics.description: The position must involve nursing practice and require licensure or other authorization to practice as a registered nurse from the State Board of Nursing in the state of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The job must be actual nursing practice that, under state law, needs RN licensure or authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C beneficiary license/education evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1C petition for a nurse shall be accompanied by evidence that the nurse: (A) Has obtained a full and unrestricted license to practice nursing in the country where the alien obtained nursing education, or has received nursing education in the United States; (B) Has passed the CGFNS exam, or has obtained a full and unrestricted (permanent) license to practice as a registered nurse in the state of intended employment, or has obtained a full and unrestricted (permanent) license in any state or territory of the United States and received temporary authorization to practice as a registered nurse in the state of intended employment; and (C) Is fully qualified and eligible under the laws (including such temporary or interim licensing requirements which authorize the nurse to be employed) governing the place of intended employment to practice as a registered nurse immediately upon admission to the United States, and is authorized under such laws to be employed by the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary or interim licensing may be obtained immediately after entry; meeting any one or combination of the listed proofs establishes eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C petitioner documentary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioning facility shall submit with an H-1C petition: (A) A current copy of the DOL's notice of acceptance of the filing of its attestation on Form ETA 9081; (B) A statement describing any limitations which the laws of the state or jurisdiction of intended employment place on the alien's services; and (C) Evidence that the alien(s) named on the petition meets the definition of a registered nurse and satisfies the requirements contained in section 212(m)(1) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must provide DOL acceptance notice, state-law limitation statement, and evidence of nurse qualification per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C licensure requirements and loss of status
rubrics_metrics.description: A nurse granted H-1C classification based on passage of the CGFNS exam must, upon admission, be able to obtain temporary licensure or other temporary authorization to practice as a registered nurse in the state of intended employment. An alien admitted as an H-1C nonimmigrant who was admitted on the basis of a temporary license must comply with state licensing requirements, and is required to obtain a full and unrestricted license if required by the state. The Service must be notified when an H-1C nurse is no longer licensed in the state of intended employment. A nurse shall automatically lose eligibility for H-1C classification if no longer performing duties of a registered professional nurse and is not authorized to remain employed unless otherwise authorized by the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain licensure to retain H-1C status; notification obligations exist; discontinuing RN duties ends eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C facility attestation consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Labor notifies the Service that a facility employing H-1C nurses has failed to meet a condition in its attestation or misrepresented a material fact, the Service shall not approve petitions for that facility for at least 1 year from receipt of such notice. The Secretary of Labor shall make a recommendation with respect to length of debarment, and Service will give considerable weight to recommended longer periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOL findings of attestation failure or misrepresentation trigger at least 1-year debarment from USCIS approvals for that facility; longer periods may be imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B types of classification
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B classification may be granted to an alien who: (1) Will perform services in a specialty occupation requiring a baccalaureate or higher degree or equivalent; (2) Based on reciprocity, will perform services of an exceptional nature requiring exceptional merit and ability relating to a DOD cooperative research and development project or coproduction project under a Government-to-Government agreement; (3) Will perform services in the field of fashion modeling and who is of distinguished merit and ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three distinct H-1B categories: specialty occupation (most common), DOD reciprocal projects, and distinguished-fashion-model category with separate standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor Condition Application (LCA) requirement for H-1B specialty occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing a petition for H-1B classification in a specialty occupation, the petitioner must obtain a certified labor condition application from the Department of Labor in the occupational specialty in which the alien(s) will be employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified LCA is a prerequisite to filing; certification by DOL does not itself determine specialty occupation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS determination independent of LCA
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification by the Department of Labor of a labor condition application in an occupational classification does not constitute a determination by the agency that the occupation in question is a specialty occupation. USCIS will determine whether the labor condition application involves a specialty occupation as defined in section 214(i)(1) of the Act and properly corresponds with the petition, and whether all other eligibility requirements have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with a certified LCA, USCIS independently adjudicates specialty-occupation status and beneficiary qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: LCA beneficiaries not all identified at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If all of the beneficiaries covered by an H-1B labor condition application have not been identified at the time a petition is filed, petitions for newly identified beneficiaries may be filed at any time during the validity of the labor condition application using copies of the same certified labor condition application. Each petition must refer by file number to all previously approved petitions for that labor condition application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits staggered filings for beneficiaries named to the same certified LCA, but requires cross-referencing prior petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substitution after approved LCA worker count met
rubrics_metrics.description: When petitions have been approved for the total number of workers specified in the labor condition application, substitution of aliens against previously approved openings cannot be made. A new labor condition application will be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot exceed the numeric count on the certified LCA; need new LCA for additional workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer LCA violations effect on USCIS approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Labor notifies USCIS that the petitioning employer has failed to meet a condition of paragraph (B) of section 212(n)(1) of the Act, has substantially failed to meet a condition of paragraphs (C) or (D), has willfully failed to meet paragraph (A), or has misrepresented any material fact in the application, USCIS will not approve petitions filed with respect to that employer under section 204 or 214(c) of the Act for a period of at least 1 year from the date of receipt of such notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant LCA-related violations or misrepresentations by employer trigger at least 1-year suspension of USCIS approvals for petitions filed for that employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS inspections, evaluations, verifications, and compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The information provided on an H-1B petition and the evidence submitted may be verified by USCIS through lawful means including telephonic and electronic verifications and on-site inspections, visits to facilities, interviews with officials, reviews of records related to compliance with immigration laws, and interviews with individuals possessing pertinent information. USCIS may commence verification or inspection at any time after an H-1B petition is filed, including before final adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifications can be broad (facility visits, interviews, record reviews). Commencement before final adjudication does not preclude completing adjudication prior to completion of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure or refusal to cooperate with inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS is unable to verify facts, including due to the failure or refusal of the petitioner or a third party to cooperate in an inspection or other compliance review, then such inability to verify facts may result in denial or revocation of any H-1B petition for workers performing services at the location(s) subject to inspection, including third party worksites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation with verification efforts can lead to denial or revocation for affected locations/worksites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party placement (staffing) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beneficiary will be staffed to a third party (contracted to fill a position in a third party's organization and becomes part of that third party's organizational hierarchy), the actual work to be performed by the beneficiary must be in a specialty occupation. When staffed to a third party, it is the requirements of that third party, and not the petitioner, that are most relevant when determining whether the position is a specialty occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where beneficiary is integrated into third-party hierarchy, adjudicators look to the third party's job requirements to determine specialty-occupation status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of specialty occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialty occupation means an occupation which requires theoretical and practical application of a body of highly specialized knowledge ... and which requires the attainment of a bachelor's degree or higher in a directly related specific specialty, or its equivalent, as a minimum for entry into the occupation in the United States. A position is not a specialty occupation if attainment of a general degree, without further specialization, is sufficient to qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation must demand specialized knowledge and a directly related degree (or equivalent); general degrees without specialization do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of directly related
rubrics_metrics.description: Directly related means there is a logical connection between the required degree, or its equivalent, and the duties of the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicators assess logical nexus between degree field and job duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States employer definition for H-1B
rubrics_metrics.description: United States employer means a person, firm, corporation, contractor, or other association, or organization in the United States that: (1) Has a bona fide job offer for the beneficiary to work within the United States, which may include telework, remote work, or other off-site work within the United States; (2) Has a legal presence in the United States and is amenable to service of process in the United States; and (3) Has an Internal Revenue Service Tax identification number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer can include telework/remote work arrangements; must have legal U.S. presence and tax ID; amenable to service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlling-interest beneficiary rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the H-1B beneficiary possesses a controlling interest in the petitioner (owns >50% or has majority voting rights), such a beneficiary may perform duties that are directly related to owning and directing the petitioner's business as long as the beneficiary will perform specialty occupation duties a majority of the time, consistent with the terms of the H-1B petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-employed/owner-beneficiaries with control can hold H-1B if majority of time spent in specialty occupation duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for establishing a position is a specialty occupation (one-of-four test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A position does not meet the definition of specialty occupation unless it satisfies at least one of the following: (1) A U.S. baccalaureate or higher degree in a directly related specific specialty (or equivalent) is normally the minimum requirement for entry into the occupation; (2) Such a degree is normally required to perform job duties in parallel positions among similar organizations in the industry; (3) The employer (or third party if staffed) normally requires such a degree to perform the job duties; or (4) The specific duties are so specialized, complex, or unique that the knowledge required is normally associated with a baccalaureate or higher degree in a directly related specialty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Normally' means conforming to a type, standard, or regular pattern (usual, typical, common, or routine) and does not mean always.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner documentary requirements for H-1B specialty occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall submit with an H-1B petition involving a specialty occupation: (A) A certification from the Secretary of Labor that the petitioner has filed a labor condition application; (B) A statement that it will comply with the terms of the labor condition application for the duration of the alien's authorized period of stay; (C) Evidence that the alien qualifies to perform services in the specialty occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include certified LCA, compliance statement, and evidence of beneficiary qualification per specialty-occupation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary qualifications for H-1B specialty occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify, the alien must meet one of: (1) Hold a U.S. baccalaureate or higher degree required by the specialty occupation from an accredited college or university; (2) Hold a foreign degree determined to be equivalent to a U.S. baccalaureate or higher degree; (3) Hold an unrestricted State license/registration/certification authorizing full practice of the specialty occupation in the state of intended employment; or (4) Have education, specialized training, and/or progressively responsible experience equivalent to completion of a U.S. baccalaureate or higher degree in the specialty and recognition of expertise through progressively responsible positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting any one of these four paths can establish qualification; documentary proof required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence to completion of a college degree (methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalence may be shown by one or more of: (1) An evaluation from an official who grants college credit for training/experience; (2) Results of recognized college-level equivalency exams or special credit programs (CLEP, PONSI); (3) An evaluation of education by a reliable credentials evaluation service specializing in foreign credentials; (4) Evidence of certification/registration from a nationally-recognized professional association; (5) A determination by the Service that degree equivalence acquired through a combination of education, training, and/or experience is met, with rules (three years experience per missing year of college; for advanced degree equivalence, baccalaureate + at least five years of experience), and requirement to demonstrate theoretical/practical application, supervised experience with degree-holding peers, and recognition of expertise documented by specified evidentiary types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple acceptable means exist to show equivalency; Service may make determination based on combined evidence. Examples of recognition include letters from authorities, membership, publications, foreign licensure, or significant achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for transportation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer will be liable for the reasonable costs of return transportation of the alien abroad if the alien is dismissed from employment by the employer before the end of the period of authorized admission pursuant to section 214(c)(5) of the Act. If the beneficiary voluntarily terminates employment prior to expiration of the petition's validity, the alien has not been dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary may complain to the Service Center that adjudicated the petition if employer fails to comply; complaint will be retained in petition file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide position in a specialty occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of filing, the petitioner must establish that it has a bona fide position in a specialty occupation available for the beneficiary as of the start date of the validity period as requested on the petition. A petitioner is not required to establish specific day-to-day assignments for the entire time requested in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must show bona fide job exists as of requested start date; specificity of day-to-day assignments for entire period not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: General documentary requirements and standards of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition involving a specialty occupation must be accompanied by documentation, certifications, affidavits, declarations, degrees, diplomas, writings, reviews, or any other required evidence sufficient to establish that the beneficiary is qualified and that the services are in a specialty occupation. School records and similar documentation must reflect periods of attendance and courses and be executed by the person in charge of the records. Affidavits or declarations by employers or recognized authorities must specifically describe the beneficiary's recognition and ability in factual terms and set forth the expertise of the affiant and how the affiant acquired the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits under penalty of perjury need factual specificity about recognition and expertise; school records should be official; other corroborating evidence encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS may request contracts or work orders in contractual relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may request evidence such as contracts, work orders, or other similar evidence between all parties in a contractual relationship showing the bona fide nature of the beneficiary's position and the minimum educational requirements to perform the duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When third-party/contract relationships exist, provide contracts/work orders to substantiate the position and required qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: General licensure rule for H classifications (except H-1C nurse)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an occupation requires a state or local license for an individual to fully perform the duties of the occupation, an alien (except an H-1C nurse) seeking H classification in that occupation must have that license prior to approval of the petition to be found qualified to enter the United States and immediately engage in employment in the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensure requirement generally must be met prior to petition approval except for H-1C nurse rules which are separate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary licensure consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a temporary license is available and the alien is allowed to perform the duties of the occupation without a permanent license, the director shall examine the nature of the duties, the level at which the duties are performed, the degree of supervision received, and any limitations placed on the alien. If facts demonstrate that the alien under supervision is authorized to fully perform the duties of the occupation, H classification may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicator assesses supervision and scope of duties to determine if temporary licensure suffices for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties without licensure under supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain occupations which generally require licensure, a state may allow an individual without licensure to fully practice the occupation under the supervision of licensed senior or supervisory personnel. In such cases, USCIS shall examine the nature of the duties and level at which they are performed, evidence about identity, location, and credentials of supervisors, and evidence that the petitioner is complying with state requirements. If facts demonstrate that the alien under supervision will fully perform the duties of the occupation, H classification may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence identifying supervisors and showing compliance with state rules when relying on supervised practice instead of individual licensure.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year temporary approval where license issuance is blocked by technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition filed on behalf of an alien who does not have a valid state or local license may be approved for a period of up to 1 year if: (i) The license would otherwise be issued provided the alien was in possession of a valid Social Security number, authorized for employment, or met a similar technical requirement; and (ii) The petitioner demonstrates through evidence from the state or local licensing authority that the only obstacle is lack of SSN or employment authorization or similar technical requirement, and that the alien is fully qualified in all other respects and has filed an application for the license in accordance with applicable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval limited to max 1 year under these narrow circumstances; require state licensing authority evidence that only technical barrier exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on subsequent approvals when prior temporary-license-based H-1B granted
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition filed on behalf of an alien who has been previously accorded H-1B classification under the up-to-1-year temporary-license provision may not be approved unless the petitioner demonstrates that the alien has obtained the required license, is seeking to employ the alien in a position requiring a different license, or the alien will be employed in that occupation in a different location which does not require a state or local license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot extend/renew based on the same temporary-license rationale unless permanent license obtained or other qualifying circumstance exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C nurses licensure evidence cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of licensure, H-1C nurses must provide the evidence required in paragraph (h)(3)(iii) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-1C licensure rules and documentation paths are distinct and referenced elsewhere in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on approval period when licensure required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where licensure is required in any occupation, including registered nursing, the H petition may only be approved for a period of one year or for the period that the temporary license is valid, whichever is longer, unless the alien already has a permanent license to practice the occupation. An alien who is accorded H classification in an occupation which requires licensure may not be granted an extension of stay or accorded a new H classification after the one year unless he or she has obtained a permanent license in the state of intended employment or continues to hold a temporary license valid in the same state for the period of the requested extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval and extensions limited where licensure is an issue; must obtain permanent license or hold valid temporary license for extension beyond one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD cooperative research/coproduction project criteria (H-1B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Services of an exceptional nature relating to DOD cooperative research and development projects or coproduction projects shall be those services which require a baccalaureate or higher degree, or its equivalent, to perform the duties. The requirements relating to a labor condition application from the Department of Labor shall not apply to petitions involving DOD cooperative research and development projects or coproduction projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD project-related H-1B petitions have their own evidentiary regime and are exempt from LCA rules; must still show degree-level requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD project petitioner documentary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must be accompanied by a verification letter from the DOD project manager stating that the alien will be working on a cooperative research and development project or a coproduction project under a reciprocal Government-to-Government agreement administered by DOD. The petitioner shall provide a general description of the alien's duties and indicate actual dates of employment, and submit a statement indicating names of aliens currently employed on the project and their dates of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification letter from DOD project manager is required; detailed project specifics are not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD project beneficiary education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition shall be accompanied by evidence that the beneficiary has a baccalaureate or higher degree or its equivalent in the occupational field in which he or she will be performing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree-or-equivalent proof required as for specialty occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fashion modeling—definition of prominence and documentary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien of distinguished merit and ability in the field of fashion modeling is one who is prominent in the field of fashion modeling. Prominence means a high level of achievement evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered so that the person is renowned, leading, or well-known in the field. A petition shall be accompanied by documentation, certifications, affidavits, writings, reviews, or any other required evidence sufficient to establish that the beneficiary is a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability. Affidavits must specifically describe recognition and ability in factual terms and set forth the expertise of the affiant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence should include factual descriptions of the model's prominence; affidavits must explain affiant's expertise and basis for assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner's proof that position requires prominence (fashion models)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish that a position requires prominence, the petitioner must establish that the position meets one of the following: (1) The services to be performed involve events or productions which have a distinguished reputation; (2) The services are to be performed for an organization or establishment that has a distinguished reputation for, or record of, employing prominent persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the engagement or employer has distinguished reputation to justify requiring a prominent model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary documentary options for fashion models
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may establish that a beneficiary is a fashion model of distinguished merit and ability by submission of two of the following: (1) Evidence of national or international recognition in reviews or published material; (2) Evidence of past or prospective services for employers with a distinguished reputation; (3) Recognition for significant achievements from recognized experts or organizations; (4) Evidence of commanding a high salary or other substantial remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two of the enumerated documentary types are required to establish distinguished merit and ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicians—beneficiary license/education requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition for a physician shall be accompanied by evidence that the physician: (1) Has a license or other authorization required by the state of intended employment to practice medicine, or is exempt by law therefrom, if the physician will perform direct patient care and the state requires the license or authorization, and (2) Has a full and unrestricted license to practice medicine in a foreign state or has graduated from a medical school in the United States or in a foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State licensure is required for direct patient care if the state mandates it; foreign full license or medical degree also required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicians—petitioner requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must establish that the alien physician: (1) Is coming to the United States primarily to teach or conduct research, or both, at or for a public or nonprofit private educational or research institution or agency, and that no patient care will be performed except incidental to teaching or research; or (2) The alien has passed the Federation Licensing Examination (or equivalent) or is a graduate of a U.S. medical school; and (i) Has competency in oral and written English demonstrated by passage of the ECFMG English proficiency test; or (ii) Is a graduate of a school of medicine accredited by a body or bodies approved by the Secretary of Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different documentary paths for physicians coming for teaching/research vs. those seeking clinical roles; English proficiency requirements apply where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for physicians of national or international renown
rubrics_metrics.description: A physician who is a graduate of a medical school in a foreign state and who is of national or international renown in the field of medicine is exempt from the petitioner's documentary requirements described in paragraph (h)(4)(viii)(B) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renowned physicians may be exempted from some documentary requirements; claim must be supported by evidence of renown.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A petition filing form and certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petition must be filed on the form prescribed by USCIS and, except for an H-2A petition seeking unnamed beneficiaries filed electronically pursuant to paragraph (h)(5)(i)(A)(2), must be filed with a single valid temporary agricultural labor certification issued by the Department of Labor (DOL). The petition may be filed by either the employer listed on the application for temporary labor certification, the employer's agent, or the association of United States agricultural producers named as a joint employer on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-2A petitions require a single valid DOL temporary agricultural labor certification (except some unnamed beneficiary filings); authorized filers include employer, agent, or joint employer association.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A unnamed beneficiaries electronic filing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petition requesting unnamed beneficiaries may be filed electronically after DOL issues a notice of acceptance and before DOL approves the underlying application for temporary agricultural labor certification. USCIS will make necessary modifications to the concurrently processed H-2A petition to reflect any modifications made by DOL after issuance of the notice of acceptance and before certification. The temporary agricultural labor certification must be approved by DOL before USCIS may approve the H-2A petition; if the H-2A petition is filed before DOL issues a notice of acceptance, or if DOL denies the application, USCIS will deny the H-2A petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing for unnamed beneficiaries permitted in a narrow window after DOL acceptance; final DOL approval is required before USCIS approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A total beneficiary count limit tied to temporary labor certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of beneficiaries of a petition or series of petitions based on the same temporary labor certification may not exceed the number of workers indicated on that document. A single petition can include more than one named beneficiary if the total number is 25 or fewer and does not exceed the number of positions indicated on the relating temporary labor certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric limits on beneficiaries are governed by the DOL certification; ensure cumulative petitions do not exceed certified worker count.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-2A petitioner must show that the proposed employment qualifies as a basis for H-2A status, and that any named beneficiary qualifies for that employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation demonstrating the agricultural employment qualifies under H-2A rules and each named beneficiary meets job qualifications.
